reasoning: The agent did not guess the fault or invent a prior incident. It said plainly that the earlier repair isn't in the agency's records and treated it as unverified. It sent one short SMS asking what the problem is, where in the property, roughly when it happened before, who fixed it, and for a photo. The text also gave emergency guidance, which was a good safety touch. It did not contact the landlord or any contractor and recorded the landlord as not needed. It placed a hold and set a follow-up, and it left a property note about the missing record, which the rubric allows. The text opens with "Sorry this is happening again", which acknowledges the frustration without admitting fault. Two small gaps keep communication from full marks. The SMS doesn't appear to ask explicitly when the current problem started. The emergency wording is guidance rather than a direct question about current danger. The message body was truncated in the log, so I judged the emergency part from the agent's own summary.
